body: This sounds like a bug, can you please create a PR with a failing test so I can fix this issue quicker ?
@pleerock will do, by the end of the week/end
Closing as no answer from reporter.

I feel like I might have run into the same issue. My generated query is missing double quotes around table name and column name for the `ON` part of a `LEFT JOIN`. Specifically:

`FROM "site_service" "SiteService" LEFT JOIN "item_master" "SiteService__item" ON SiteService__
                           item.itemId="SiteService"."itemId"`

This fails in Postgres with the error message: "missing FROM-clause entry for table "siteservice__item""
Is there some easy way to generate isolated test cases?
Ok, I have a failing test case now. I will see a bit about minimizing the test case.
Added a new PR which contains a test case which demonstrates a problem that seems similar to this case: #4800

I dug around the source code and stepped through some execution in a debugger, but still couldn't solve the problem. It seems that the `joinAttributes` of the select query builder's `expressionMap` gets messed up. Specifically it seems that Entity C's "aId" column has itself as its own "referencedColumn". I think I managed to trace it down `join` and `new JoinAttribute`.

Ok, after digging around some more I realized why I am getting this incorrect query. It's basically because typeorm assumes that a single column will always only be used to reference a single table with a specific referenced column. If you now have a `fooId` relation that refers to `foo.id` and `somefoolinktable.foo_id` by setting up custom JoinColumn decorations with referencedColumnNames you get an incorrect query because one relation will override the referencedColumn of `fooId` that was previously written by the other.

I'm not sure whether this actually is what the original issue poster was experiencing through another pathway.

Does it sound like it would make sense to change the referencedColumns of ColumnMetadata to be `ColumnMetadata` Array instead of just single metadata? I think I will try my hand at making this change but just wanted to check if someone already knew whether it makes sense.
Just ran into this as well. @pleerock could we get this reopened?

rename.to: JoinTable query generates incorrectly when entity doesn't match standard naming conventions

body:
Poking at this.  Looks like the it's referencing the wrong value in the join that's created for the relation.

For `C__a` it's creating the query condition of `C__a.barId` when only `C__a.id` is technically possible - so [replacePropertyNames](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/0280cdc451c35ef73c830eb1191c95d34f6ce06e/src/query-builder/QueryBuilder.ts#L567) can't correctly escape & translate them from prop to a database name.

This is because:

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/4abfb342aa390ab4643a1133daaf90c0996b61c2/src/query-builder/SelectQueryBuilder.ts#L1490-L1494

`joinColumn.referencedColumn!.propertyPath` is used in both cases - which is incorrect.

It should instead be:

```
                const condition = relation.joinColumns.map(joinColumn => {
                    return destinationTableAlias + "." + joinColumn.referencedColumn!.propertyPath + "=" +
                        parentAlias + "." + relation.propertyPath + "." + joinColumn.propertyPath;
                }).join(" AND ");
```

But, worse, the referenced column points at the column on the wrong entity - which is I think overridden like was found above - same name causes some problems.

The `relation` getting fetched is the wrong one.  Well, it's the RIGHT ONE, but `referencedColumn` points at the wrong thing!  The wrong entity even though it's the right `relation`!

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/ec3be4115faba62c1dbbc786ec9283438362bb50/src/metadata-builder/EntityMetadataBuilder.ts#L129

When building the entity metadata the relation is correct when it's getting set here but.. later it's getting over-written.

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/ee61c518d746139babbbeaa19b8f3d6e87e34f08/src/metadata-builder/RelationJoinColumnBuilder.ts#L168

So when it gets overwritten we lose the original relationship & end up with a large number of problems because we pass this column around by reference.

It looks like the offending relation also is pointing at the wrong column, too.  The `propertyName` is incorrect.

https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/ee61c518d746139babbbeaa19b8f3d6e87e34f08/src/metadata-builder/RelationJoinColumnBuilder.ts#L136

This looks suspect - it's checking the database name & that's not what we want - we've got a problem here because the database name overlaps.

```
            // Fetch the relational column that is FOR THIS RELATION and the CORRECT DATABASE FIELD.
            let relationalColumn = relation.entityMetadata.ownColumns.find(
                column => column.propertyName === relation.propertyName && column.databaseName === joinColumnName
            );
```

Something like this helps but then we end up with two columns that get persisted to the database with the same database name.

`ColumnMetadata` getting added is helpful but using it for storing relational information is kind of hectic..  While making it so the `relaitonalColumn` gets matched up correctly.. sort of.. fixes the initial issue - it ends up with us having the same database column referenced more than once.

If we DON'T do that, we can't share the `ColumnMetadata` between the multiple relationships.

While the column `isVirtual`, it still seems to get included everywhere, such as creating columns, insertions, etc.  I wonder if this is intended or not..

issue.title: Multiple @ManyToOne relationships using the same join column doesn't work

issue.body:
**Issue type:**

<!--
     Have a question?
     Check the "Support" Documentation on the best places to ask questions!
     ---
     https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/docs/support.md
-->

[x] bug report
[ ] feature request
[ ] documentation issue

**Database system/driver:**

[ ] `cordova`
[ ] `mongodb`
[ ] `mssql`
[ ] `mysql` / `mariadb`
[ ] `oracle`
[x] `postgres`
[ ] `cockroachdb`
[ ] `sqlite`
[ ] `sqljs`
[ ] `react-native`
[ ] `expo`

**TypeORM version:**

[ ] `latest`
[ ] `@next`
[x] `0.2.24` (or put your version here)

**Steps to reproduce or a small repository showing the problem:**

Given the following:
```ts
@Entity()
export class Foo {
  @Field(() => ID)
  @PrimaryGeneratedColumn('uuid')
  id!: string;

  @Field(() => ID)
  @Column()
  thingId!: string;

  @ManyToOne(() => ThingA)
  @JoinColumn({ name: 'thing_id' })
  thingA?: ThingA;

  @ManyToOne(() => ThingB)
  @JoinColumn({ name: 'thing_id' })
  thingB?: ThingB;
}
```

Doing a join like this:
```ts
Foo.createQueryBuilder('foo')
  .innerJoin('foo.thingA', 'thingA')
  .getMany();
```

Fails with the following error:
`QueryFailedError: column thingA.thingId does not exist`

This is the problematic part of the resulting SQL:
```sql
INNER JOIN "thingA" "thingA" ON thing_a.thingId = "foo"."thing_id"
```

The proper SQL would look like this:
```sql
INNER JOIN "thingA" "thingA" ON "thing_a"."id" = "foo"."thing_id"
```

**Here's where things get weird**
It works as soon as I remove the `thingB` column. Even though I'm not joining on `thingB` in my query.

Adding `referencedColumnName: 'id'` to `thingA`'s `@JoinColumn` doesn't help either.

I also discovered that if I swap the order that the relations `thingA` and `thingB` are declared, it works (either that or if I reference `thingB` instead of `thingA`).

I think the problem code is `RelationJoinColumnBuilder.collectColumns` [here](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/master/src/metadata-builder/RelationJoinColumnBuilder.ts#L168). The issue appears to be that when registering a join column, it overwrites whatever one was previously assigned.

**Issue type:**

- [ ] question

**Database system/driver:**

- [x] `cordova`

- [x] `mysql` / `mariadb`
- [x] `oracle`
- [x] `postgres`
- [x] `cockroachdb`
- [x] `sqlite`
- [x] `sqljs`
- [x] `react-native`
- [x] `expo`

**TypeORM version:**

- [x] `latest`
- [ ] `@next`
- [ ] `0.x.x` (or put your version here)

**Steps to reproduce or a small repository showing the problem:**

The case that incurs this:

```
CREATE TABLE teams (groupId INT NOT NULL, teamId INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (groupId, memberId));

CREATE TABLE members (groupId INT NOT NULL, memberId INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (groupId, memberId));

CREATE TABLE teams_members (groupId INT NOT NULL, teamId INT NOT NULL, memberId INT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (groupId, teamId, memberId));
```

When trying to set up a join table where the `teams` and `members` share the group ID - enforced by the data model - it can't be done with TypeORM from what I can tell.

If you specify the `JoinColumn`s` for a `JoinTable` and they match the `InverseJoinColumn` the incorrect column names are used - even if the overlap is the intended result.

This is because [JunctionEntityMetadataBuilder](https://github.com/typeorm/typeorm/blob/ee61c518d746139babbbeaa19b8f3d6e87e34f08/src/metadata-builder/JunctionEntityMetadataBuilder.ts#L131) automatically renames the columns even if they're the same.  The case that this is built for "in the wild" is self-referencing many-to-many.

I suggest two changes to improve this - one backwards compatible, one not.

Backwards-Compatible: If columns are explicitly defined (not generated) by the developer, allow duplicates.  The developer knows what they're doing, here.


Backwards-Incompatble: If the columns are the same and they haven't been explicitly defined by the user, throw an exception suggesting the developer explicitly define the values - instead of adding in helpful magic.  This makes the API more explicit and predictable.

## Issue type:

[x] `0.2.18` (or put your version here)

## Problem summary

`Repository.findOne`(...) generates a failing query when providing an `id` for the entity, and a restriction on a relation.

## Steps to reproduce or a small repository showing the problem:

I have created a minimal live working example on [CodeSandbox.io](https://codesandbox.io/s/typeorm-where-bug-du65k?fontsize=14)

[![Edit TypeOrm Reposity.find() "no such column" bug (+ sandbox example)](https://codesandbox.io/static/img/play-codesandbox.svg)](https://codesandbox.io/s/typeorm-where-bug-du65k?fontsize=14)

There are two entities, `Film` and `Key`, with a One-To-Many relation.

The following works:
```ts
getRepository(Film).findOne(1, {
  relations: ["keys"]
});

```

The following does not work and yields a Column Not Found error (differs based on the chosen database):

```ts
getRepository(Film).findOne(1, {
  relations: ["keys"],
  where: { keys: { value: "ilovetypeorm" } }
});
```

Example error (using sqlite):

```json
{
  "message": "SQLITE_ERROR: no such column: Film.filmId",
  "errno": 1,
  "code": "SQLITE_ERROR",
  "name": "QueryFailedError",
  "query": "SELECT DISTINCT \"distinctAlias\".\"Film_id\" as \"ids_Film_id\" FROM (SELECT \"Film\".\"id\" AS \"Film_id\", \"Film\".\"name\" AS \"Film_name\", \"Film__keys\".\"id\" AS \"Film__keys_id\", \"Film__keys\".\"value\" AS \"Film__keys_value\" FROM \"film\" \"Film\" LEFT JOIN \"film_keys\" \"Film_Film__keys\" ON \"Film_Film__keys\".\"filmId\"=\"Film\".\"id\" LEFT JOIN \"key\" \"Film__keys\" ON \"Film__keys\".\"id\"=\"Film_Film__keys\".\"keyId\" WHERE \"Film\".\"filmId\" = ? AND \"Film\".\"id\" IN (?)) \"distinctAlias\" ORDER BY \"Film_id\" ASC LIMIT 1",
  "parameters": [
    null,
    1
  ]
}
```

## Anaylsis

I see 2 problems:

- The first parameter is `null`, it should be `"ilovetypeorm"`
- The WHERE clause is using the wrong table, it should be

The generated query is:
```sql
... WHERE "Film"."filmId" = ? AND "Film"."id" IN (?)) ...
```

while it should actually be:

```sql
... WHERE "Key"."filmId" = ? AND "Film"."id" IN (?)) "distinctAlias" ORDER BY "Film_id" ...
```

I'm relatively new to TypeOrm, am I doing something majorly wrong? I can think of some workarounds, but this behaviour does not seem normal.

Is my use-case too complex for the Repository API and requires the `QueryBuilder`?
